term-life.name: Term Life Insurance
term-life.shortDescription: Affordable coverage for a specific period — 10, 15, 20, or 30 years.
term-life.longDescription: Term life insurance provides a death benefit to your beneficiaries if you pass away during the policy term. It is the most straightforward and affordable type of life insurance. You pay a fixed premium for a set number of years, and your family receives a tax-free payout if you die while the policy is active. Most term policies can be converted to permanent coverage without a new medical exam.
pros: Level premiums for the entire term
cons: Coverage expires at end of term
No return of premium unless rider added

whole-life.name: Whole Life Insurance
whole-life.shortDescription: Permanent lifetime coverage with a cash value component that grows tax-deferred.
whole-life.longDescription: Whole life insurance provides coverage for your entire life, as long as premiums are paid. A portion of each premium payment goes into a cash value account that grows at a guaranteed rate. You can borrow against or withdraw from the cash value tax-free. The premium, death benefit, and rate of return are all guaranteed, making whole life insurance a stable long-term financial tool.
cons: Slower cash value growth vs. investments

health.name: Health Insurance
health.shortDescription: Comprehensive medical coverage for individuals and families, including ACA-compliant plans.
health.longDescription: Health insurance helps cover the cost of medical care, including doctor visits, hospital stays, prescription drugs, and preventive care. Plans are available through employers, the ACA marketplace, Medicaid, and Medicare. Key terms to understand include premiums, deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and out-of-pocket maximums. Choosing the right plan depends on your expected healthcare utilization and budget.

auto.name: Auto Insurance
auto.shortDescription: Financial protection for your vehicle and liability in case of accidents.
auto.longDescription: Auto insurance provides financial protection if you are involved in a car accident or your vehicle is damaged. State laws require minimum liability coverage, but full coverage options include comprehensive (theft, weather) and collision (accidents). Rates are determined by driving record, vehicle type, location, age, and credit score in most states.
cons: Can be expensive for young drivers
Comprehensive coverage may exceed car value
bestFor: New car owners needing full coverage

home.name: Home Insurance
home.shortDescription: Protection for your home, personal belongings, and personal liability.
home.longDescription: Homeowners insurance protects your home's structure, your personal belongings, and provides liability coverage if someone is injured on your property. Mortgage lenders typically require homeowners insurance. Standard policies cover damage from fire, theft, wind, and other named perils. Flood and earthquake coverage typically require separate policies.
pros: Temporary living expenses if home uninhabitable
